source.note: Notes were removed from library/bible/WEB at conversion (2026-06). They are kept here, apart from the verse text, as the translators wrote them. Built by tools/build-web-notes.py.

notes.text: "Jesus" is a Greek variant of the Jewish name "Yehoshua," which means "Yah saves." "Jesus" is also the masculine form of "Yeshu'ah," which means "Salvation."

notes.text: The word for "wise men" (magoi) can also mean teachers, priests, physicians, astrologers, seers, interpreters of dreams, or sorcerers.

notes.after: those who collected the didrachma coins
notes.text: A didrachma is a Greek silver coin worth 2 drachmas, about as much as 2 Roman denarii, or about 2 days wages. It was commonly used to pay the half-shekel temple tax, because 2 drachmas were worth one half shekel of silver.

notes.after: its mouth, you will find a stater coin.
notes.text: A stater is a silver coin equivalent to four Attic or two Alexandrian drachmas, or a Jewish shekel: just exactly enough to cover the half-shekel Temple Tax for two people.

notes.after: o him who owed him ten thousand talents.
notes.text: Ten thousand talents represents an extremely large sum of money, equivalent to about 60,000,000 denarii, where one denarius was typical of one day's wages for agricultural labor.

notes.after: vants, who owed him one hundred denarii,
notes.text: 100 denarii was about one sixtieth of a talent.

notes.after: agreed with the laborers for a denarius
notes.text: A denarius is a silver Roman coin worth 1/25th of a Roman aureus. This was a common wage for a day of farm labor.

notes.after: He went out about the third hour,
notes.text: Time was measured from sunrise to sunset, so the third hour would be about 9:00 AM.
